articles.title: ‘We don’t need people like that on earth’: Parisians on the riots that shook France
articles.description: Subhead:One week after a student protest turned into looting and fires across France, I went to Place de la République to ask Parisians who did it and what comes next.# YouTube-embed:avbeRujyO5s I was in Paris on October 24, near Place de la République. A week earlier, on Saturday, October 17, a student protest there turned into a riot, with shops looted and burned in Paris and in other cities across France. A woman who lives in the neighbourhood told me she supported the march but not the looters. “I was mostly sad for the shopkeepers,” she said. A man said he understood the anger but not the destruction. “They steal sneakers, they steal alcohol, they smash the PMU bar next door. You have to shout, but not like that.” An elderly man who served in a commando unit in the 1950s said that back then, they opened fire. “There were deaths, fine, but they didn’t do it again.” When I asked who did the looting, people split. “Angry people, poor people,” one resident said. “Nobody steals for pleasure.” An older man disagreed. “They’re people from elsewhere, madame. People who are here to wreck things.”
